newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - DSM 1996 net seen down sharply.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - DSM 1996 net seen down sharply.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM is seen reporting sharply lower net profits when it releases provisional 1996 earnings figures next Tuesday.
Analysts are forecasting a fall in net profits to some 728-790 million guilders from a year-earlier 1.07 billion, due mainly to a margin squeeze in hydrocarbons and polymers.

The consensus net profit estimate stands at 750 million guilders, including a 10 million guilder extraordinary charge taken in the first 1996 quarter. In 1995, extraordinary charges amounted to two million guilders.
"The main pressure on group profits will come from the hydrocarbons and polymers activities," said Peter Schouten, chemicals analyst with merchant bank MeesPierson.
Schouten, who is forecasting full-year 1996 net of 740 million guilders, said higher prices for the raw materials it uses to make plastics had cost DSM dear.
"Over the whole year, DSM will have lost an estimated net 120 million guilders due to higher oil and naphtha prices," Schouten said.
Nils van Elzelingen of broker NIB Strating also pointed to a lower result for hydrocarbons and polymers, saying margins on ethylene and polyethylene were much lower than in 1995.
Van Elzelingen is forecasting full-year net profits of 764 million guilders, and rates the stock an underperformer.
"I will be more interested to hear what DSM has to say about the future -- we are clearly rather less optimistic than some of our colleagues on prospects," Van Elzelingen said.

He said recent full-year profit figures from Union Carbide Corp of the U.S. indicated continued pressure on margins in hydrocarbons and polymers. "I think plastic prices will remain weak in 1997," he added.
DSM's other divisions are generally seen turning in an improved performance, but this will not be enough to offset the sharply lower result at hydrocarbons and polymers, analysts say.
Van Elzelingen said he expected base and fine chemicals would boost operating profits to 552 million guilders from a year-earlier 476 million.

Base chemicals had suffered as prices for synthetic fibre intermediates had plummeted on slack demand, but the acquisition of Chemie Linz -- finalised in early 1996 -- would have improved the result in fine chemicals, he said.
Results at resins and plastic products were seen improving as the market recovered and the division reaped the benefits of restructuring.
A 60-40 joint venture with BASF in the field of unsaturated polyester resins would also have boosted profitability, Van Elzelingen said.
DSM is set to release a provisional 1996 net profit figure on Tuesday, with full results to follow on Tuesday, February 25.
